unit: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
summary: Lead engineer for CLARO, a multimodal agentic decision-support system for civic policy analysis.
highlights: Lead engineer for CLARO, which dynamically decomposes user queries into dependency-aware execution DAGs spanning reasoning, retrieval, analysis, and stakeholder-analysis capabilities.
Architected a planner-driven orchestration layer with 7+ registered capabilities, with bounded parallelism, dependency scheduling, timeouts, and failure isolation.
Integrated LLM tool use and RAG-based structured evidence retrieval returning typed, source-grounded results.
Designed a progressive WebSocket-based interaction architecture that streams completed results while synthesis and speech generation run asynchronously.
Benchmarked CLARO on historical civic-deliberation records, achieving ~75% stakeholder-conflict coverage.
Developing StakeBench and SchemeBench to study synthesis-layer bias in multi-agent systems.
Investigating when self-reflection improves LLM reasoning, using counterfactual paired trajectories and hidden-state probes to predict reflection utility beyond uncertainty-based triggers.
Studying language-model reliability and interpretability through internal representations, behavioral evaluation, and intervention-based analysis across reasoning tasks.
Conducted mechanistic interpretability research on negation and epistemic uncertainty in biomedical language models.
Investigated privacy-preserving and affect-adaptive language modeling through prompt stylometry.

summary: Asset-management modernization and LLM-assisted reporting for a leading wind and solar energy producer.
highlights: Modernized a legacy stand-alone asset management system into a RESTful web application, improving system reliability and reducing downtime by 35%.
Built a RAG-based asset-health reporting system, synthesizing unstructured maintenance and operational logs into standardized reports and reducing manual reporting effort by 40%.
Automated critical data synchronization pipelines via scheduled jobs, improving data integrity and eliminating 75% of manual synchronization effort.

summary: Core modules, data pipelines, and ML services for a B2B2C digital insurance platform serving 10,000+ daily active users.
highlights: Engineered core modules for an integrated B2B2C digital insurance platform serving 10,000+ DAU across policy, partner, and operations management.
Contributed to the platform's shift from D2C to B2B2C, helping reduce partner onboarding from ~5 months to ~30 days through API-driven carrier and partner integrations.

Architected AWS-based ETL pipelines processing ~50M records annually with automated ingestion, monitoring, and failure recovery — reducing manual operational intervention by 95% and reclaiming 250+ engineering hours annually.
Engineered an XGBoost lead-prioritization engine with feature-level explainability over multi-source customer data, supporting ~15% QoQ growth and ~$30M in incremental premium volume.
Migrated REST endpoints to GraphQL, reducing network payload size by 60%.
Strengthened platform security by managing dependencies, reducing vulnerabilities, and supporting SOC 2 compliance initiatives.
